item: Row J: the curated stamp writes through one UPDATE per chunk and one INSERT
summary: stamp_curated_catalog wrote three attributes per row through the ORM and added one attempt row each (one INSERT statement per row on a first install). It now issues one ORM-enabled bulk UPDATE per 400-id chunk (update(Source) through session.execute), guarded by status = 'unqualified' so a row another writer moved after the scan is neither overwritten nor given an attempt row, and one executemany INSERT of the attempt rows. The rows left are identical to the ORM form column for column (tests/test_curated_stamp_batched.py keeps the old form as the reference). The ORM form also rewrote feed_key from rss_url on every row it touched, through the J1 before_update mapper event, which a bulk UPDATE does not fire: the stamp now repairs a stored key that disagrees with its own rss_url for the rows it stamps, with the same function, in one executemany by primary key and nothing on a healthy store. Bulk DML through session.execute still reaches do_orm_execute, so the single-writer gate and write marker see both statements. Export's independent re-measure of this function (keyword-export/stamp-curated-remeasure-2026-10-17/REPORT.md section 8; the app's own engine and session, connection already open, 3 rounds x 6 warm runs, a fresh process per cell): 0.138 s plain [0.127..0.185] and 0.148 s encrypted [0.136..0.192]; against the old per-row form in the same session (quiet pass) 0.822 s to 0.147 s plain and 0.935 s to 0.154 s encrypted, -82 % and -84 %. The feed_key check costs +0.016 s plain and +0.020 s encrypted (13 to 16 %), inferred to be Python work and not profiled inside the function. The first call in a process still pays about 1 s of catalogue parse, with or without the change. Not probed: a stored key that is non-blank and wrong, and the heal on an encrypted store.
